root_cause.text: The MPU-3050 gyroscope driver called iio_device_register() before completing all necessary initialization steps (trigger setup, power management configuration), creating a race condition where userspace could access the device before it was fully ready.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves `iio_device_register()` from before trigger and PM runtime initialization to the end of the probe function, and correspondingly moves `iio_device_unregister()` to the start of the remove function. The commit message explicitly states "iio_device_register() should be at the end of the probe function to prevent race conditions."

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: The MPU-3050 gyroscope driver called iio_device_register() before completing all necessary initialization steps (trigger setup, power management configuration), creating a race condition where userspace could access the device before it was fully ready.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch moves `iio_device_register()` from before trigger and PM runtime initialization to the end of the probe function, and correspondingly moves `iio_device_unregister()` to the start of the remove function. The commit message explicitly states "iio_device_register() should be at the end of the probe function to prevent race conditions."

candidates.rationale: This is the direct call to iio_device_register(), which exposes the device to userspace before trigger and power management initialization are completed, creating a race condition.
This statement sets the device driver data after registration, meaning userspace callbacks that rely on dev_get_drvdata() may fail or access stale data before this is set.
Power management configuration is performed after registration, leaving the device in an inconsistent power state for userspace consumers that may access it immediately.
This rpm put is part of the power management setup that should have been completed before the device is registered to prevent premature runtime suspend transitions.

This statement sets the device driver data after registration, causing userspace callbacks that rely on dev_get_drvdata() to fail or access stale data until this is set.
Power management configuration (autosuspend) is performed after registration, leaving the device in an inconsistent power state for userspace consumers that may access it immediately.
This runtime PM put is part of power management setup that should have been completed before device registration to prevent premature runtime suspend transitions.
